# You don’t have to be a developer to benefit from vibe coding


Vibe coding can help you solve everyday work problems, save time and build useful tools—even if you don’t have a software development background.


Published Oct 02, 2026


D


ByDaniel Patterson


Published Oct 02, 2026


## At a glance


-


**Easier app building:** Vibe coding uses natural-language prompts to help you build apps and other useful tools with AI, even if you don’t have a software development background.


-


**Where to begin:** Start with a problem you understand, give AI a clear goal and be upfront about what you don’t know. Then test and refine your prompts as you go.


-


**Work more efficiently:** Save processes that work so you can reuse them to tackle new challenges, automate repetitive tasks and spend more time on higher-value work.


What if the solution to an everyday problem could come from an app, but it didn’t take new software, a developer or a months-long project to develop that app? And what if it was something you could easily build yourself?


That’s the promise of vibe coding, an AI capability that allows you to create software using natural-language prompts: You describe what you want an app to look like and do, and AI helps write the logic, structure and user interface. From automating repetitive tasks to building simple AI tools that make a process easier, vibe coding can give people in all kinds of roles a new way to approach problems at work.


I discovered just how useful vibe coding could be after taking several AI courses offered to me—and all other Verizon employees—by Verizon and earning the Google AI for Professionals certificate. Those courses are now available for free to anyone via[Verizon AI Skills for America](https://www.verizon.com/about/responsibility/human-prosperity/workforce-development/ai-learning?utm_source=pace-aisfa-stories&utm_campaign=default&utm_medium=default) .


I’m a principal managing sales engineer at Verizon, but I’m not a software developer. (In fact,[63% of vibe coding users identify as non-developers](https://keyholesoftware.com/vibe-coding-trends-2026/) .) Though I studied web development, I haven’t actually coded since 2014. The training I took showed me that anyone can learn this skill. It introduced me to app scripting and vibe coding, and once I learned how to prompt AI effectively, I started experimenting with what I could build.


One of the first big problems I tackled was something our sales teams had struggled with for years: making our business communications platform easier for customers to visualize. In less than a week, I used vibe coding to build an interactive drag-and-drop tool that lets teams map a customer’s setup in real time. That tool has since been used by teams across Verizon, allowing me to reach a much broader audience and scale my impact.


Since then, I’ve kept experimenting with vibe coding for work and for my personal benefit. Here are some of the lessons I’ve learned about how to vibe code that can help you put the skill to work in your own job.


## 1. Start with a problem you want to solve


Look at your day-to-day and find something you think you could improve. It doesn’t need to be big—just something to get started with.


My first vibe coding project wasn’t the drag-and-drop tool. I do a lot of training and enablement, and I wanted something more engaging than another slideshow. I decided to see if I could create a Jeopardy-style training game. That gave me a low-stakes way to experiment. Once I saw what was possible, I started thinking about bigger problems I already understood—and that led me to create the sales tool.


**What to keep in mind:** You bring the subject-matter expertise. You know where the friction is and what a better outcome would look like. AI can help you explore how to get there.


## Build your AI skills with free training from Verizon.

## 2. Tell AI what you don’t know


One of the first things I had to learn was how to communicate with AI effectively. Being upfront about what I didn’t know actually made that easier. I would give the AI my end goal, explain what I wanted to build and what resources I had, and ask it to walk me through the process step by step.


Then I experimented. Vibe coding is a test-and-learn experience: Try something, see what happens, troubleshoot and refine your instructions. The more I did it, the better I became at communicating what I needed and knowing what to ask next.


**What to keep in mind:** If you can copy, paste and converse, you can win.


## 3. Save what works and refine your vibe coding process


As I got better at vibe coding, I realized I shouldn’t start over every time.


I began saving prompts that worked. I created a coding partner prompt, an instructional command you give to the AI to get it to act more like a collaborative programming partner, that establishes best practices for how I want it to work with me. I also built a branding prompt that provides the parameters I need to follow.


**What to keep in mind:** Don’t duplicate your efforts. When you find something that works, save it, refine it and use what you learned on the next problem.


## 4. Give yourself time back


Not every useful AI solution needs to be an app. Sometimes the best problem to solve is simply a time-sucking task.


I regularly create executive summaries that once required me to manually find numbers and compile information from reports. That could take an hour. Now I can use AI to help generate the summary in minutes, and then I only need to verify the numbers for accuracy.


The time I get back allows me to focus more on enablement—helping other people learn and succeed—which is the part of my job I’m most passionate about.


**My best advice:** After taking an AI course, make sure you do something with what you learned. You don’t have to be a developer to benefit from vibe coding. You just need to start looking at the problems around you and asking what you might be able to build.

What AI tools can I use for vibe coding?


A growing number of AI tools can help with vibe coding, including general-purpose AI assistants and dedicated AI coding platforms. Different tools offer different capabilities, so beginners should consider what they want to build, ease of use, cost and any workplace requirements before choosing one.


What can you use vibe coding for at work?


Vibe coding can help you build practical tools such as calculators, dashboards, training games, workflow automations and interactive prototypes that solve everyday problems or make tasks more efficient.


Is vibe coding safe to use at work?


Vibe coding can be useful at work, but employees should follow their organization’s policies for AI, data privacy and security. Avoid entering confidential or sensitive information into an AI tool unless it has been approved for that purpose, and always test and review AI-generated outputs before putting them to use.
